title: Celsus’s Jew; disciples and circumcision mission (chs. 1–20)
english: Book II opens after Book I’s personified Jew against Jesus. Origen answers the Jew’s charge that disciples deserted the law, citing Jesus’ word to Peter and the mission among the circumcised, and refuses the claim that the Gospel stories are clumsy fictions.
translator_notes: Copy-text Koetschau GCS 2–3 Perseus TEI; no Chadwick/ANF Crombie.
True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B; condensed book CLOSEOUT.
Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Prophecy, passion, and empty tomb disputes (chs. 21–40)
english: The Jew presses passion and empty-tomb stories as inventions; Origen holds that prophecy and the disciples’ later boldness fit a risen Lord better than a fabricated corpse-theft tale.
translator_notes: Copy-text Koetschau GCS 2–3 Perseus TEI; no Chadwick/ANF Crombie.
True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B; condensed book CLOSEOUT.
Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Moses’ wonders vs Jesus; consistency of Scripture (chs. 41–60)
english: If Celsus’s Jew trusts Moses’ wonders as from God, he cannot dismiss Jesus’ works by a double standard. Scripture’s own tests of true and false signs must be applied evenly.
translator_notes: Copy-text Koetschau GCS 2–3 Perseus TEI; no Chadwick/ANF Crombie.

title: Jew’s epilogue — BOOK II CLOSEOUT (chs. 61–79)
english: The Jew’s closing word calls Jesus a mere man exposed by the facts; Origen answers that the epilogue restates the earlier insults without proving them, and closes Book II.
